articles.title: Two automakers change security systems two hours after alerted of vulnerability
articles.author: Teresa Moss

paras.en: Two automakers changed their security systems within hours after a team of hackers notified them of a vulnerability that allowed remote access to unlock and start the automakers’ vehicles.

Shubham Shaw and Sam Curry, white hat hackers, found vulnerabilities on ForgeRock servers that allowed them access to customer logins for two automakers, according to a Nov. 7 post from the hackers. White hat hackers look for vulnerabilities in systems before the weakness can be used for malicious purposes.
The post doesn’t identify the automakers.
The affected system served customers in multiple regions, but the hackers say they only tested U.S. accounts and vehicles.

“In the past few years, we’d found ways to remotely control vehicles from Honda, Acura, Nissan, Infiniti, Hyundai, Genesis, Ford, Porsche, Kia, and Subaru, but we’d never found a vulnerability that enabled remote access to either an Automaker #1 or Automaker #2 vehicles,” the post states.

Once in the app, the hackers say they could see every vehicle VIN that the owner had in their garage, along with its location, mileage, fuel, battery range, tire pressure, door and window state, vehicle health, alerts, and subscription status.

According to the hackers, they first downloaded the Android version of the apps for both automakers and traced their authentication flows back to ForgeRock. The post describes ForgeRock as an identity platform used by both automakers to manage customer accounts and logins.

In the post, the hackers identified a series of steps they took to disable and enter the security system. This included replacing credentials and changing a user’s email and password to log in to ForgeRock.

“Changing the email address and password did not invalidate the account owner’s existing app session,” the post states. “During our authorized test, the owner’s app remained logged in while our new session worked alongside it.”
According to the hackers, they dug deeper into the identity stack than they originally expected.

“Production identity access extended across the affected directories for both automakers in multiple regions, and we validated the complete account-to-vehicle chain with live US accounts and vehicles,” the post adds.
The hackers accessed the vehicles in early 2026, the post states. The automakers were also notified of the vulnerability via a report provided to their product security teams in early 2026.
“Both automakers remediated the vulnerability approximately two hours after receiving the report,” the post states. “The proof bundle was removed, and the affected credentials were rotated.”
During a July Collision Industry Conference (CIC) meeting, Andrea Amico, Privacy4Cars founder and CEO, said the average car in the past 10 years has about 250 sensors.
“Cars have become the third personal computing device that consumers use every day,” he added.
However, vehicles typically lack encryption or hidden controls compared to phones or computers, he said.
Vehicles can collect personal data through cameras, microphones, GPS, and synced phones, he said. Data collected by vehicles includes call logs, garage codes, biometrics, contacts, and passwords.
During a separate CIC presentation, Tracy Dombrowski of Collision Advice provided an example of a woman who sold her vehicle to a dealer without disconnecting it from her app.

“She was able to follow that vehicle from the sale of the vehicle to Florida to Texas,” Dombrowski said. “She is still able to remote start that vehicle; she is still able to access that vehicle at any given time.”
The job of data removal typically falls on the consumer, she said. But shops can help consumers as a courtesy.
Dombrowski provided OEM webpages that offer resources for removing PPI.

articles.title: Nasdaq chief economist: Inflation will likely fade and interest rates will lower
articles.author: Lurah Lowery

paras.en: Phil Mackintosh, Nasdaq chief economist and senior vice president, painted a picture of a resilient economy during the annual MSO Symposium held Nov. 2 and shared his predictions for the year ahead, including lower interest rates.

Mackintosh said the markets have “powered through” three big challenges over the last year: tariffs, the war in Iran, and interest rate changes. There are no recessions in the world, and “growth might be slow, but it’s positive enough to weather the shocks like we’ve been seeing,” he said.

“We’re definitely seeing the economy sort of turn around; things get more positive or less negative depending on which side of the economy you’re on,” Mackintosh said. “And because of that, in the labor market, we are starting to see a little bit of strength. [At] the start of the year, this was meant to be a really good tailwind for the stock market and a really good tailwind for company profits. It turns out the tailwind is still happening. Hiring is starting to pick back up.”
According to Mackintosh, tariffs didn’t create a big dent in the global economy, and have somewhat stabilized.
“Initially there was that huge spike in the average tariff rate. It’s actually been coming down,” he said.
Interest rates have also generally been coming down.

“They didn’t affect the economy as much as you think, even though for a lot of companies they definitely created a lot of uncertainty,” he said. “In terms of your industry, whether tariffs have impacted inflation much… the answer is not much at all.”

“The general trend in this industry in inflation is you’re on a deflationary trend, and now you’ve become deflationary, so the impact of tariffs from this industry onto the CPI [Consumer Price Index] actually is pretty small,” he said.

Effects on the oil market from the Iran War were digested much better than might’ve been expected, according to Mackintosh. He said that despite 20 million barrels a day missing from global supply, and the biggest shock to oil supply caused by wars dating back to the 1950s, the price of oil didn’t go up that much.
And that doesn’t seem to be getting better when looking at shipping data, he noted.
“The war is still active from an economic and supply perspective,” Mackintosh said.

As for interest rates, he said they have gone from definitely falling to definitely rising, if you trust the market, and the reason for that is inflation. Mackintosh said interest rates are now hiking quickly because the Federal Reserve waited so long for transitory oil-driven inflation to go away.

“The Fed is not sitting there going, ‘Well, oil prices could easily come down to $70 or $60 if we resolve the war and the supply chain fixes,'” he said. “Instead, the Fed is trying to slow the economy down just in case.”
And long-term borrowing is starting to cost consumers and companies money, he said. Several developed countries, in addition to the U.S., have seen long-term interest rates increase.

“If interest rates and debt both go up, they both add to the amount of costs that we’re all going to have to pay out of our tax receipts or tax bills, so you can see net interest costs becomes bigger and bigger as a problem,” Mackintosh said.
He noted that households are trying to stretch how long they’ll own a car, increasing the number of months on a new car loan.
“It’s going up and up and up as people try to buy a car that’s going to last longer than the usual cycle,” he said.

Mackintosh called himself a contrarian for his prediction that interest rates will be lower in 12 months. He said worsening Middle East conflict causing real supply shock would be the only reason his prediction would be wrong.

“I actually think we’re more likely to see inflation fade,” he said. “If the conflict in Iran doesn’t get worse, then the oil price won’t keep going up, which means it stops being inflationary. Imagine if it goes away and the oil price comes down, then you get deflation from oil, and all of a sudden we could be talking about 2% inflation pretty quickly.”
Another deflationary factor is the aging population against a shrinking workforce.

“There’s more people retired than there are with babies needing new houses and new cars and more clothes, so the demand kind of comes out of the economy,” Mackintosh said. “Interest rates don’t need to be very high in an economy where the population is shrinking.”
Much more risk would be in play if the heat came out of the economy naturally and inflation decreased on its own, he added.
Mackintosh said layoffs near historic lows are one facet that has helped the economy. Meanwhile, hiring has softened.

“We have what we’re calling a ‘no hire, no fire’ market, so everyone feels pretty secure, but the job creation slowed down quite a lot,” he said. “People that are unemployed and staying unemployed is starting to fall, so that’s good news as well. People are actually getting into work slowly rather than seeing people lose jobs.”
Tariffs, he added, are basically done, and the price increases they caused are last year’s story. Mackintosh predicts tariff increases won’t show in the CPI in a couple more months.
Mackintosh also covered the AI boom and its effect on the national and global economies. He predicts that AI could become deflationary if it makes us more productive.
According to his data, Mackintosh said AI capital expenditures are a large proportion of what’s currently driving the U.S. gross domestic product (GDP).

“The stock market basically reacted to AI this year rather than to the economy,” he said. “AI as a sector is contributing more and more to that growth in GDP, and so it’s become a really important economic factor to the market and the economy as a whole.
Chip demand will be much higher than ever because of the high demand for data centers, along with a phenomenal demand for electricity, Mackintosh added.
For example, he said that the Meta data center being built in Louisiana needs about 30% of the electricity the state currently produces.
“This is why it’s driving the economy too, though,” he said, adding that with AI there are “a lot of known unknowns.”

“We are still building AI; we’re still making it work in products,” he said. “We’re still trying to work out what it really can deliver. On the positive side, you’ve got the growth in token volumes or the growth in actual AI queries. It just keeps going up. …the revenues have started to plateau.

“I think from an economic perspective, there’s plenty of reasons to say that it’s worth all of us doing this. And the reason I say that is if you look at the internet boom, there was a heap of CapEx, almost the same kind of scale of CapEx to the GDP in the ’90s when we were building out the internet. All the connectivity they created, the fact that we can have CarPlay in our cars and GPS, all that cool stuff is because of the internet.”
He predicts the companies that will benefit from AI might be building products we haven’t imagined.
Featured image: Phil Mackintosh, Nasdaq chief economist and senior vice president, speaks during the 2026 MSO Symposium on Nov. 2. (Lurah Lowery/Repairer Driven News)

articles.title: NTN Holds Community Spirit & Engagement Event
articles.author: Alex Crissey

paras.en: NTN Bearing Corp. of America held its Community Spirit & Engagement Event at the Elk Grove Township Food Pantry in Elk Grove Village, Illinois, on Tuesday, October 27. A team of twelve NTN employees volunteered to help combat food insecurity and support local families ahead of Thanksgiving.

Volunteers spent the morning assembling approximately 400 Thanksgiving food bags that will be distributed to families throughout the community. Designed as a “trick-or-treat” style shopping experience, team members worked together at various food stations, collecting and packing items including cooking oil, canned vegetables, canned pumpkin, mashed potatoes, macaroni and cheese, gravy, brownie mix, and other household necessities.

In the afternoon, NTN employees assisted pantry staff with organizing and storing five pallets of donated food. According to the food pantry manager, the work completed by the NTN team in a few hours would have taken the pantry’s regular staff and volunteers up to a month to accomplish.

NTN’s Community Spirit & Engagement Program, launched in January 2023, includes contributing time and resources to charitable organizations, encouraging employees to take an active role in the local community, and building partnerships with other groups and organizations.

The Elk Grove Township Food Pantry provides food assistance and related support services to residents facing food insecurity, serving approximately 1,100 families each month through a client-choice model that allows households to access nutritious food and household essentials in a dignified and convenient manner. Through partnerships with community organizations, donors, and volunteers, the pantry helps ensure local families have access to the resources they need throughout the year and is expected to distribute the Thanksgiving food bags assembled during the event to nearly 900 families this holiday season.

articles.title: Understanding the Tesla FSD System
articles.author: Andrew Markel

paras.en: Tesla’s Full Self-Driving (FSD) system can steer, accelerate, brake, change lanes and navigate many roads, but the driver remains responsible for the vehicle. Technicians will need to keep this in mind because a customer report may describe either an expected operating limitation or a condition that needs diagnosis.

System behavior also varies by model, year, hardware and software version. FSD is available on some Cybertruck, Model 3, Model S, Model X, and Model Y vehicles. Always confirm the applicable VIN-specific service information before performing service.

FSD (Supervised) uses the vehicle’s cameras to build a model of the surrounding area. The vehicle’s computer processes that input and uses it to make driving decisions. Depending on the software and vehicle configuration, FSD can follow road curves, respond to traffic lights and stop signs, make turns, change lanes, navigate highway ramps and roundabouts, and follow a route to a destination. The touchscreen displays a visualization of some detected road users and objects, but that display is not a complete representation of every input the system uses.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: The driver can set a destination or allow the vehicle to select a likely route. Speed-profile settings influence speed and lane-change frequency. FSD can be engaged from a stop or while driving, subject to system availability and vehicle conditions. During operation, it may slow for traffic, stop at traffic controls, maneuver around a vehicle partially blocking the lane when space allows, and make lane changes without requiring driver confirmation. The driver can intervene at any time by steering, braking, accelerating or disengaging the system.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: The cabin camera monitors driver attentiveness while FSD is engaged. If the system detects repeated inattention or the driver does not respond to prompts, it can issue escalating warnings and suspend access. Repeated ignored warnings may count as strikeouts and temporarily disable FSD. A driver-initiated disengagement is expected and is not, by itself, improper use.

Before diagnosing a complaint, establish what the vehicle was doing, where it was, the software version, the selected speed profile, the camera and road conditions, and whether the driver received a warning. Confirm that the system was enabled and available, and inspect the touchscreen for messages. Check for clean, unobstructed cameras and current map data. Rain, snow, fog, direct sun, darkness, faded lane markings and camera obstruction can limit performance. A rear-mounted hitch accessory, bike rack or trailer may block a camera or degrade function.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Some unavailability is expected. FSD may not engage if the driver is not seated with the seat belt fastened, a door or frunk is open, a charge cable is connected, the tailgate is down, or the vehicle is in a mode that restricts the feature. On the Cybertruck, headlights must be set to On or Auto; FSD may disengage or be unavailable if they are Off. A camera obstruction or incomplete calibration can also prevent use.

FSD may need immediate driver intervention on narrow roads, at complex intersections, around construction, during unprotected turns with fast cross traffic, in heavy-traffic merges, near debris, or when road curvature is high. Interactions with pedestrians, cyclists and other road users can also require intervention. The vehicle may brake, steer or change lanes unexpectedly, even when conditions appear straightforward. Visibility is especially important, and poor weather or lighting can significantly degrade performance.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: A complaint that the system is unavailable during one of these conditions may reflect a limitation rather than a failed component. The same may be true if the driver was repeatedly prompted to look at the road, apply slight steering force or take over. If FSD disengages, the driver should receive an alert and chime; determine whether the reported event was a normal disengagement, a warning that went unanswered, or a repeatable fault.

Do not dismiss every report of unexpected behavior as normal. Tesla’s warnings require the driver to supervise, but they do not establish that every maneuver is acceptable. Ask for the exact location, route, road markings, signal state, weather and time of day. Check available vehicle alerts, camera status, calibration state, software and service history. A report of proceeding against a red light, entering an opposing lane or taking a wrong-way turn deserves careful documentation and escalation under applicable service procedures.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: One note: NHTSA opened a preliminary evaluation in October 2025 covering an estimated 2.88 million FSD-equipped vehicles after reports of traffic-law violations, including red-light entry and travel against the proper direction. The agency said it would assess FSD’s ability to detect signals, lane markings and wrong-way signs, along with the warnings and response time provided to drivers. NHTSA notes that an investigation is not a recall determination.
Camera Calibration and the 100-Mile Drive

Camera calibration may be required before some self-driving features are available for the first time or after certain repairs. Cybertruck owner information says calibration usually completes after about 20 to 25 miles, although distance varies with conditions. Clear lane markings, multiple visible lanes, a straight road and light traffic help the process complete. The manual recommends a multi-lane highway, preferably with several lanes and clear markings.

After camera or windshield service, or if a camera has shifted from its calibrated position, the procedure directs the technician to clear calibration through Controls > Service > Camera Calibration > Clear Calibration. The vehicle then repeats its self-calibration process while being driven. Confirm the camera and windshield installation, camera view and relevant service work before the road test; clearing calibration does not correct a physical obstruction or misaligned camera.

Monitor the touchscreen for calibration progress and feature-availability messages. If calibration has not completed after approximately 100 miles driven in suitable conditions, the Cybertruck owner information says to schedule service. Treat 100 miles as the point at which continued failure merits diagnosis. The menu path, conditions and calibration logic can vary by model and software, so verify the procedure for the vehicle being serviced.

Calibration is not a substitute for verifying camera position. If the camera or windshield was replaced, inspect the mounting and optical path and follow the applicable service procedure. A camera that is physically out of specification may repeatedly fail to calibrate or provide unreliable input even after the software calibration has been cleared.

The supplied forward-facing camera pitch procedure is labeled a draft, although it says it has been validated. Confirm the latest procedure and applicability by VIN before starting; do not treat its steps as universal to every Tesla model.

If performing this adjustment on a Cybertruck, the procedure calls for setting ride height to Medium, placing the vehicle in Service Mode, unlocking the Gateway and parking on a flat surface with at least 3.5 feet of clearance in front. Position the camera calibration target against the front fascia, centered on the vehicle, with its bottom 3 feet from the ground. Verify the target is level, then apply red tape at the specified 165-centimeter reference height.

In the touchscreen’s Service Mode, open Driver Assist > Cameras > Camera Preview > Pitch Verification > Main Camera > Wide Camera. Review the main and wide camera images. The top of the tape should align with the blue horizontal line; if it falls between the green lines, pitch is within specification.

If adjustment is required, remove the rearview-mirror beauty cover. The procedure then directs the technician to clear camera calibration, reset DAS and ping DAS using the specified Service Mode Plus functions, followed by adjustment with the pitch-adjustment wrench. Clockwise rotation pitches the camera upward; counterclockwise rotation pitches it downward. Tesla’s procedure states that one rotation can change pitch by approximately 0.5 to 1.5 degrees. Re-check the camera images and repeat the adjustment until the reference falls within the green lines. Reinstall the cover, remove the target, exit Service Mode and complete any required calibration. Use the specified tools and follow the full current procedure, including its safety precautions.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Two recalls are especially relevant to FSD and camera service. In 2023, recall 23V-085 covered certain Model S, Model X, Model 3 and Model Y vehicles equipped with FSD Beta. The recall addressed certain driving maneuvers that could violate traffic laws or customs; Tesla’s remedy was an over-the-air software update. Recall 23V-489 covered certain 2023 Model S, Model X and Model Y vehicles with forward-facing camera pitch outside specification, which could make certain active-safety features unavailable without alerting the driver. The remedy was inspection and, if needed, pitch adjustment. Check recall status by VIN and confirm completion before diagnosing related complaints.

articles.title: AI & the Aftermarket: AUMOVIO’s Stefan Feder
articles.author: Mary DellaValle

paras.en: AftermarketNews asked executives from leading manufacturers/suppliers about how their companies are using artificial intelligence, what problems they hope to solve and how they see AI impacting their business in the coming years. It is our pleasure to share their insights and, today, we hear from Stefan Feder, Head of Automotive Aftermarket, North America, AUMOVIO Systems, Inc.
How is your company currently using artificial intelligence?

At AUMOVIO, we are applying AI across the value chain, from engineering and product development to manufacturing, knowledge management, and overall business processes. Our objective is not simply to automate existing work. It is to improve how quickly knowledge moves through the organization, how confidently decisions are made, and how effectively expertise can be scaled. This value-creating approach is true for AUMOVIO at large as well as for our aftermarket business. And to name just one example, we are currently exploring AI-supported technical assistance that could help technicians access trusted product and service information more quickly, and at the same time ensure that we do not lose the human touch that we consider very critical for the aftermarket industry. The governing principle is important: AI provides speed and scale, while people provide judgment, accountability, and context. The real opportunity comes from combining both.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Do you believe AI will change the competitive landscape of the aftermarket?

At first, the aftermarket is and will remain a people driven industry, and AI will not change that. Nevertheless, AI will have an impact on our industry as it will on many other industries. AI will change how the aftermarket makes decisions, and it can improve key performances, but it will not replace the fundamentals. It will make product quality, trusted data, technical expertise, and customer confidence even more important. The winners won’t be the companies with the most AI tools. They’ll be the ones that turn expertise and data into better decisions and performance. And ultimately become brands that both customers and AI systems confidently recommend.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Looking ahead three to five years, where do you see AI having the greatest impact on the aftermarket?

Besides further efficiency gains and helping technicians keep increasingly complex vehicles safely on the road, the greatest impact will be at the point of decision. In the short-term, AI has already started to support identifying the right part with less searching and uncertainty. Over time, the decision maker may not always be a person. A connected vehicle could recognize a service need, communicate with a repair facility and parts will be selected and procured autonomously. In that environment, the aftermarket must prepare for both human and machine customers. Our industry and the future will remain exciting, that’s for sure.

articles.title: The Case for Fewer SKUs
articles.author: Jeff White

paras.en: Every automotive parts store faces the same inventory challenge: having the right parts available without tying up too much capital. With thousands of SKUs competing for limited shelf space, finding the right balance isn’t easy.
Bill Nunnery, senior director, sales and marketing, Global Aftermarket at Dana Incorporated, believes SKU consolidation can help stores address that challenge while improving customer service.
“The one challenge that every distributor is faced with is having the right part at the right place at the right time,” Nunnery said.
Inventory management involves more than keeping shelves stocked. Stores must also consider how much working capital they invest in inventory and whether those products generate sufficient sales.

Nunnery said the industry has little tolerance for slow-moving inventory, particularly as shelf space becomes increasingly valuable. Carrying similar products from multiple suppliers can further complicate inventory management. Reducing redundant SKUs can help stores control costs while simplifying the purchasing process.
“And so minimizing the complexity and choices is always a good thing for the customer,” Nunnery said.
That means fewer overlapping options to navigate while helping customers identify the appropriate products for their applications.

Counter pros see firsthand which products customers request most often and which alternatives can serve multiple applications. That experience can provide valuable insight into inventory decisions, particularly when stores evaluate overlapping products or identify opportunities to simplify their assortments.
Nunnery pointed to Dana’s Reinzosil universal sealing compound as an example of how SKU consolidation can benefit parts stores and repair shops.

According to Nunnery, one tube of Reinzosil can replace 10 to 12 conventional RTV sealant varieties. That allows distributors to reduce inventory requirements while offering a product that serves multiple applications.

The benefits extend into the repair bay. A technician might otherwise keep 10 or 12 different tubes of RTV sealant in a toolbox. Those tubes take up space, and their contents have a limited shelf life.
“You’ve got to remember this is a perishable item,” Nunnery said.

Consolidating those products into one sensor-safe solution can simplify inventory management for technicians while reducing the number of individual products they must purchase and maintain. The same principle applies at the parts store.

Nunnery noted that an automotive retailer or independent parts store might dedicate 10 to 12 linear feet of shelf space to RTV products. He estimated that consolidating the category around a universal solution could reduce merchandising requirements by 70% to 80%. That would free valuable space for other products without requiring additional shelving or warehouse capacity.

Of course, reducing SKUs shouldn’t come at the expense of product availability or application coverage. Nunnery emphasized that distributors must evaluate consolidation opportunities with their customers’ needs in mind.
“I think when they’re deciding on consolidation, I think it always, again, it starts with the customer first,” he said.

That philosophy should guide inventory decisions throughout the distribution chain. Manufacturers and distributors can use category management analytics to identify opportunities to reduce inventory while maintaining appropriate application coverage.

Ultimately, successful SKU consolidation requires collaboration between manufacturers and distributors. The objective isn’t simply to stock fewer products. It’s to reduce unnecessary complexity, make better use of available resources and ensure customers can get the products they need.
For parts stores, that’s a strategy that can benefit both sides of the counter.

articles.title: A widely used antibiotic for acne and infections is linked to risk of pregnancy loss, new study finds
articles.author: Isha Ishtiaq

paras.en: Taking doxycycline, a commonly prescribed antibiotic, during the first trimester of pregnancy may increase the risk of pregnancy loss, a new study suggests.

The antibiotic is broad-spectrum, meaning it targets a wide range of bacteria. It's often used to treat acne, respiratory infections and sexually transmitted infections, such as chlamydia and syphilis. Doctors generally avoid prescribing the drug during the second and third trimesters because it belongs to a class of antibiotics that can bind to calcium in developing bones. Animal studies suggest that this may disrupt fetal bone development.

However, evidence on doxycycline's safety during early pregnancy has been mixed and limited. The new study, published Tuesday (Nov. 10) in the journal Annals of Internal Medicine, provides clearer evidence of a link between doxycycline use in the first trimester and pregnancy loss.

"I would advise physicians to carefully consider the benefit-risk balance when prescribing doxycycline to women who are pregnant or planning a pregnancy," study first author Almut Winterstein, a pharmacist and drug-safety researcher at the University of Florida, told Live Science in an email.

Using information from two U.S. insurance databases, the researchers analyzed 224,870 pregnancies in people ages 12 to 55. More than 218,230 of these patients were treated for respiratory tract infections, and over 6,630 were treated for acne, between conception and the end of the first trimester. About 4,385 of the women filled a prescription for doxycycline during that time frame, while the others received an alternative antibiotic.

Among women with respiratory infections, those prescribed doxycycline had a 40% to 54% higher risk of pregnancy loss, compared with those prescribed amoxicillin, another broad-spectrum antibiotic in a different class. The exact level of risk varied between the two databases.

The researchers also compared the doxycycline users against women prescribed macrolides, the class of antibiotics that includes azithromycin (or "Z-Pak"). Again, the doxycycline users saw a higher risk — 39% and 36% higher, respectively.
Get the world’s most fascinating discoveries delivered straight to your inbox.

Among the patients treated for acne, doxycycline users had a 49% higher risk of pregnancy loss in one database than those given the antibiotic clindamycin. In the second database, though, the difference wasn't statistically significant. Winterstein said that may be because there were fewer patients included in that analysis.
Overall, doxycycline was associated with seven to 11 additional pregnancy losses per 100 pregnancies, compared with the other antibiotic options assessed, the researchers reported.

It is not yet clear how the drug might contribute to pregnancy loss. Because the study was observational, it cannot prove that the antibiotic itself caused those losses, which included miscarriages and stillbirths. (Miscarriage is pregnancy loss before 20 weeks of pregnancy, whereas stillbirth refers to pregnancy loss after the 20th week.)

Animal studies hint that doxycycline could interfere with early placental development, potentially making it harder for the placenta to support a growing pregnancy, Luke Grzeskowiak, an associate professor and clinical pharmacist at Flinders University in Australia who was not involved in the study, said in an email.

The study authors also noted in their report that the drug may have direct effects on the developing embryo. But these explanations remain hypothetical; the researchers have not established that either mechanism occurs in humans.

"Pregnancy loss affects around one in four pregnancies and can happen for many reasons," Grzeskowiak noted. Although doxycycline exposure may add to that risk, taking the antibiotic does not necessarily mean pregnancy loss will occur. The available data suggests that it is just one risk factor among many.

Because doxycycline may be prescribed before a pregnancy is recognized, doctors should consider the possibility of pregnancy when prescribing this drug to women of reproductive age, particularly those who are sexually active, Grzeskowiak suggested. That does not mean doctors should avoid prescribing the antibiotic to these women, he emphasized; rather, clinicians should consider pregnancy plans and medical history when choosing a treatment.

In some cases, doxycycline may still be the best option for a severe infection, Winterstein told Live Science, and that infection could itself put a pregnancy at risk. But for less-serious infections, safer alternatives may be available, she said.
This article is for informational purposes only and is not meant to offer medical advice.

Winterstein, A. G., Chen, H., Thai, T., Wang, Y., Smolinski, N. E., Wen, W., Ewig, C. L., Gilboa, S. M., Meaney-Delman, D., Maro, J. C., & Rasmussen, S. A. (2026). Doxycycline and risk for pregnancy loss: A multi-database, multi-indication cohort study. Annals of Internal Medicine. https://doi.org/10.7326/annals-26-01647

Isha Ishtiaq is a freelance health journalist based in Pakistan who covers health, medicine and biomedical research. Her work has appeared in Live Science, Science News, and Medscape, among other outlets. She holds a B.S. (Hons) in biotechnology from the University of Gujrat and an M.S. in biological sciences from the University of Sialkot, where her research focused on the use of deep learning models for disease detection.

articles.title: Chinese scientists cool atoms to near absolute zero in record-breaking experiment
articles.author: Elizabeth Howell

paras.en: Scientists have cooled atoms to the coldest temperature ever recorded, using a laser trap aboard China's Tiangong space station.

Tiangong included an experiment in which atoms were cooled to 10 picokelvins, which is barely above absolute zero, the coldest theoretical temperature possible in physics. Absolute zero is minus 459.67 degrees Fahrenheit (minus 273.15 degrees Celsius) and the threshold at which all particles in an object are believed to stop moving.
Scientists hit the mark using "optical tweezers," known more formally as an optical-dipole trap (ODT), which hold atoms in a laser beam," the scientists reported Nov. 5 in the journal Science.

The team placed 20,000 rubidium atoms in the trap in order to restrict their motion. This reduced motion, along with the weightlessness induced by the low-gravity environment aboard the space station, caused the cloud of atoms to cool to much lower temperatures than are possible on Earth.
The experiment's results could help improve future space-based research, the team said.
"This record-low temperature could stimulate a new generation of ODT-based experiments in quantum simulation and precision measurements in space," the researchers wrote in the paper.

Despite this achievement, it's doubtful that scientists could ever hit absolute zero. One interpretation of the third law of thermodynamics, which looks at how systems behave when they approach absolute zero, is that the particles would always have a bit of entropy (disorder) associated with them, making absolute zero unachievable.
Get the world’s most fascinating discoveries delivered straight to your inbox.

"One version of the third law states that it would require an infinite number of steps to reach absolute zero, which means you will never get there," Saibal Mitra, a professor of physics at Missouri State University, told Live Science in a 2024 interview.

The second law of thermodynamics, which states that entropy always increases, would also be violated if scientists could reach absolute zero, he added. "If you had a heat sink at absolute zero, then you could build a machine that was 100% efficient," Mitra said.

That said, space makes it easier to get close to absolute zero because microgravity allows atoms to "float" and become more efficient at cooling, Science News reported. The researchers took their weightless collection of atoms and created a quantum state of matter known as a Bose-Einstein condensate, in which very cold atoms clump and create a "fifth state" of matter as they behave akin to a single atom.

Tiangong's very cold clump follows similar experiments on the International Space Station that reached 52 picokelvins and from a weightless fall induced by a drop from a tall tower, in which atoms hit 38 picokelvins, Science News added.

Quantum gases below 10 picokelvin in space. Science, eaea5324. https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aea5324

Elizabeth Howell was staff reporter at Space.com between 2022 and 2024 and a regular contributor to Live Science and Space.com between 2012 and 2022. Elizabeth's reporting includes multiple exclusives with the White House, speaking several times with the International Space Station, witnessing five human spaceflight launches on two continents, flying parabolic, working inside a spacesuit, and participating in a simulated Mars mission. Her latest book, "Why Am I Taller?" (ECW Press, 2022) is co-written with astronaut Dave Williams.

articles.title: 'Like writing and directing your own movie': Live Science readers share whether they'd learn to lucid dream if they could
articles.author: Nicoletta Lanese

paras.en: Lucid dreaming describes when you realize you're in a dream as it's unfolding. Sometimes, people can control the content of their dreams from this state of awareness.
paras.zh: 清醒梦是指在梦境展开的过程中，您意识到自己正在做梦。有时，人们可以从这种意识状态控制梦境的内容。

paras.en: Recently, researchers claimed that they found a way to "train" people to lucid dream by having them meditate and complete virtual-reality-augmented exercises while they were awake. Following the release of that study, Live Science asked its readers whether they would learn to lucid dream if they could.
paras.zh: 最近，研究人员声称，他们找到了一种“训练”人们进行清醒梦的方法，即让他们在清醒时冥想并完成虚拟现实增强的练习。该研究发布后，《科学日报》询问读者，如果可以的话，他们是否愿意学习清醒梦。

paras.en: Over 300 readers weighed in, with 77% saying "Yes, I'd want to try to control my dreams." Additionally, 17% of respondents said "No, I already lucid dream enough without training," 3% said "No, I don't see the point," and the final 3% said they weren't sure.
paras.zh: 超过300名读者参与了投票，其中77%的人表示“是的，我想尝试控制自己的梦境”。此外，17%的受访者表示“不，我不用训练就已经有足够的清醒梦了”，3%的受访者表示“不，我看不出有什么意义”，最后的3%的受访者表示他们不确定。

paras.en: In the comments, one reader shared that they'd once experimented with hypnagogic napping, a technique famously used by Thomas Edison and Salvador Dalí in which the famous luminaries would wake themselves up just as they were drifting to sleep. Edison claimed that this helped him access a creative sweet spot at the edge of sleep and wakefulness.
paras.zh: 在评论中，一位读者分享说，他曾尝试过入睡前小睡法，这是一种托马斯·爱迪生和萨尔瓦多·达利都曾使用过的著名技巧，这两位名人会在即将入睡时唤醒自己。爱迪生声称，这帮助他在睡眠与清醒的边缘找到了一个激发创意的最佳状态。

paras.en: "When I was experimenting with the hypnagogic state (using the Edison method) I started having spontaneous lucid dreams," the reader wrote. "I can confidently say, that there were some of the most profound experiences of my life, so the answer is definitely yes."
paras.zh: 这位读者写道：“当我尝试入睡状态（使用爱迪生方法）时，我开始出现自发的清醒梦。” “我可以自信地说，这些是我一生中最深刻的体验，所以答案绝对是肯定的。”

paras.en: Another reader reported having lucid dreams "about once or twice a year," adding that they typically wake up shortly after realizing it's a dream. "My most recent one was of my recently deceased wife. I became very sad when I realized she wasn't supposed to be there," the reader wrote. "I hugged her and told her I don't want to be without her. She replied that I could live a long life if I took care of myself (This was a very typical response from her...lol). I feel very blessed to have had that dream."
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Other readers chimed in on Facebook. "Already have it [lucid dreaming], but if I didn't I would certainly practice to do so," one wrote. "Hell yes," another said, in response to the idea of training themselves to lucid dream.
paras.zh: 其他读者也在Facebook上发表了看法。“我已经有了[清醒梦]，但如果我没有，我肯定会练习这样做。”一位读者写道。“当然愿意。”另一位读者在回应训练自己进行清醒梦的想法时说道。

paras.en: Other readers noted that they already lucid dream quite often or that they can consistently control their dreams, with one even saying that all of their dreams are lucid. Another said, "Some nights I interrupt it [my dream] like Monty Python — 'Too silly!' and start over."

But while one person compared lucid dreaming to "writing and directing your own movie," another noted that "lucid dreams can be boring, repetitive, annoying." So while many people would practice lucid dreaming if they could, not everyone sees the appeal.

Nicoletta Lanese is the health channel editor at Live Science and was previously a news editor and staff writer at the site. She is a recipient of the 2026 AHCJ International Health Study Fellowship, with a project focused on antibiotic stewardship practices in Japan and the U.S. They hold a graduate certificate in science communication from UC Santa Cruz and degrees in neuroscience and dance from the University of Florida. Beyond Live Science, Lanese's work has appeared in The Scientist, Science News, the Mercury News, Mongabay and Stanford Medicine Magazine, among other outlets. Based in NYC, she also remains involved in dance and performs in local choreographers' work.
